# New house renderings introduced in odyssey-025 (Odyssey 5.291–387)

For folding into `conventions.md`'s house-renderings table at publication.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| καὶ τότ’ [Name] λύτο γούνατα καὶ φίλον ἦτορ (5.297; cf. the shipped τῆς δ’ αὐτοῦ λύτο γούνατα καὶ φίλον ἦτορ, 4.703) | "And then [Name]’s knees were loosed, and his/her dear heart," | "And then [Name]’s knees gave way, and his/her heart too," | "his strength failed", "his spirit sank", "his heart melted" (each drops the concrete knees, which are the image); "limbs" for γούνατα; `l` and `i` follow the wording shipped at 4.703 |
| ὀχθήσας δ’ ἄρα εἶπε πρὸς ὃν μεγαλήτορα θυμόν (whole-line introduction to a speech made to oneself, 5.298 = 5.355) | "and, vexed, he then spoke to his own great-spirited heart:" | "and, troubled, he spoke to his own great-spirited heart:" | "deeply moved", "in anguish", "groaning" (ὀχθέω is 'be vexed, troubled', shipped as "greatly vexed" / "greatly troubled" for μέγ’ ὀχθήσας at 4.30, 4.332); "said to himself" (drops θυμός); "great-hearted" (reserved for μεγάθυμος) — μεγαλήτωρ keeps "great-spirited"; kept apart from the fixed κινήσας δὲ κάρη προτὶ ὃν μυθήσατο θυμόν ("and, shaking his head, he spoke to his own heart:") |
| ὤ μοι ἐγὼ δειλός (5.299) / ὤ μοι ἐγώ (5.356) (cries of distress opening a speech) | "Oh me, I, miserable one," / "Oh me, I …" (ἐγώ is part of the cry; at 5.356 `l` joins it to the fear-clause: "Oh me, I fear …") | "Oh me, miserable that I am," / "Oh me," | "Ah" / "Ah me" (reserved for ὢ πόποι), "Alas" (archaic, and it would swallow several distinct cries), "Woe is me" (archaic), "Poor me" (childish); δειλός is "miserable", kept apart from δύστηνος ("wretched", 1.55) and from λευγαλέος ("pitiful", below) |

## Flags for the reviewer (not silently resolved)

- **5.300–302 is one unit across an ano teleia (the one deliberate break from the tap-unit rule in this part).** The half-line after the ano teleia in 302, τὰ δὲ δὴ νῦν πάντα τελεῖται., is word for word a whole published unit at 2.176 (odyssey-006). The packet did not list it, because it matches only half a line. That published unit ends Halitherses' speech, so its `l`/`i` carry a closing ” ("…being fulfilled.”" / "…coming to pass.”"). Cut here as its own unit, the validator would force exactly that English, stray ” and all, into the middle of Odysseus' speech. Any other English would fail the build. I therefore joined 300–302a and 302b into one three-line unit ending at the full stop. The half-line inside keeps the 2.176 wording without the ”, under the rule for a line that repeats inside a larger unit. The alternative is to split the unit and ship the stray ”; the reviewer or owner may prefer that. The general problem (a repeated unit whose shipped English carries speech marks that do not fit the new context) may need a line in `conventions.md`.
- **Whole-line repeats honoured.** At 5.365 (= 4.120), 5.376 (= 5.285) and 5.387 (= 2.352), each line sits inside a longer unit and keeps its published wording for that line. The internal repeats 5.298 = 5.355 and 321b = 372b, and the repeated phrases αἰθυίῃ ἐικυῖα (337, 353) and κρήδεμνον … ὑπὸ στέρνοιο τανύ- (346, 373), have the same English each time.
- **Disputed or uncertain, stated as such in the notes:** αἰθρηγενέτης (passive vs. active), αὐδήεσσα (exact force), αἴθυια (bird unknown), ὀνόσσεσθαι κακότητος at 379 (force of ὄνομαι with the genitive; taken ironically, 'you will not complain of too little evil'), Αἰγαί (which place), the subject of ἤλασε at 367 (Poseidon or the wave), δεινόν at 314 (adjective with κῦμα or adverb), σύν at 293 (adverb or tmesis).
- **Odysseus names Zeus** at 304 as the maker of the storm Poseidon raised. The note says so and does not "correct" him.
